create.title: Flat unbalanced prescribed-centre product-window and curvature envelope
create.statement_tex: Let D=X^delta and L=X^ell in the strict smooth unbalanced M2 residual region, and retain one frozen flat smooth component of the literal prescribed-centre wave R_(D,L)(X), including q_L, W, chi_4, the real centre, and the accepted stationary normalization. Then |R_(D,L)(X)|<<_epsilon X^epsilon min(D/L, sqrt(XL/D)+sqrt(X/(LD))). The first term follows from Abel summation and a real-centre integer-product layer cake; the second follows by resolving chi_4 on the full integer lattice, applying weighted second-derivative summation to Xk/r+/-r/4, and then taking the k-triangle with the exact k^(-1) mass. If a=delta-ell, the exponent is beta(a)=min(a,(1-a)/2). This saves X^((3a-1)/2) over divisor capacity exactly when a>1/3, but beta(a)>1/4 at every strict point 1/4<a<1/2. The bound is not character-specific and does not cover sharp, starred, clipped, hard, arithmetic-owner, or transition kernels.
create.next_action: Use this only as the sharp certified one-dimensional envelope for the flat wave. A continuation must save jointly in r and k before the k-triangle, or control the entire sparse selector and complement by a new inverse theorem.

create.title: Central-run and integer phase-one coherent-sector countermodel obstruction
create.statement_tex: For the same literal flat-smooth prescribed-centre wave, the exact centre and a half-integer tie are divisor-bounded. Suppose U consecutive d asymp D select r_d in one fixed odd residue class mod 4 and |X-dr_d|<=cD/L for a sufficiently small central-lobe constant. There is C_0 such that U<<1+(D^3/(XL))^(1/2) when D^3>=C_0X and U<<1+(D^4/(XL))^(1/3) when D^3<C_0X. The mod-4 lattice gap forces r_d affine or quadratic, and separated divided differences give the two bounds; both are uniformly O(X^(1/4)L^(-1/2)+X^(1/9)L^(-1/3)). Separately, on a uniformly smooth interior stationary cell and for integer X=bA^2 with b squarefree, the complete leading phase-one sector e(sqrt(Xknu))=1 has O_epsilon(sqrt(M)X^epsilon) modes and contributes O_epsilon(sqrt(D/L)X^epsilon). For X=A^2 its literal chi_4-weighted square-sector count is O(sqrt(M)); the unsigned upper bound is O(sqrt(M)log(2L)). These results rule out the listed coherent subsets as target-sized countermodels but do not control unions of runs, nonzero coherent phases for arbitrary real X, stationary transitions, endpoints, remainders, noncentral shoulders, or the complete signed complement.
create.next_action: Do not seek a lower bound from one central same-sign run, the exact centre, a tie, or the integer phase-one square sector. Any countermodel or upper bound must control all disconnected selectors, coherent phases, shoulders, and the signed complement in one literal norm.
